newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia expects 24 trln roubles from new vodka rule.
newsitem.headline: Russia expects 24 trln roubles from new vodka rule.

text.p: The Russian government could raise 24 trillion roubles a year by clamping strict controls on the production and sale of alcohol, allowing it to pay off overdue pensions, Interfax news agency quoted Finance Minister Alexander Livshits as saying on Monday.
The crackdown was decided last week by a special commission set up to deal with tax evasion and huge delays in the government's payment of wages and pensions.
President Boris Yeltsin's press service said he will sign a decree soon to enforce payment of duties and taxes by distillers, importers and retailers.
Interfax quoted Livshits as saying Russia was losing about seven trillion roubles from tax-free business with neighbouring Belarus.
Smugglers, moonshiners and bootleggers are estimated to be cheating the state of about two trillion roubles ($350 million) a month.
The new order will be based on tight controls from the gates of Russia's approximately 700 distillers and strict licensing rules for producers, sellers and importers.
Government officials said the whole business of vodka imports from Belarus and Ukraine, which used to enjoy duty-free trade with Russia, would be reviewed.
